name: gardner in rounds where swaps collide
description: Martin Gardner's 5x5 minichess played in rounds: both players move at once. Each round each player chooses one move in secret, and both moves are revealed and made together. There is no check: the king is simply captured, and the side that loses its king loses. Only two pieces moving onto the same square collide, and then both are removed. Two pieces that try to take each other in the same round meet half-way as a collision and both are removed, kings included, so striking back at an attacker that strikes is mutual destruction. A piece that moves onto a square its target has just left for somewhere else lands there if it could move to an empty square; a pawn's diagonal capture, which cannot land on an empty square, misses and the pawn stays. If both kings fall in the same round, or anything else ends the game for both players at once, the game is drawn. A round counts as two moves on the clocks. Games are short: a king can no longer strike back at an attacker that strikes, so a queen that reaches a king usually ends the game within a few rounds, often with both kings gone.

provenance.preview: A preview: a new kind of game in which both players move at once, still being tested. Play it against the computer for practice; it is on no leaderboard yet, and its score is a first reading, not yet trusted.
